top_choice_rationale: P003 (Autor, Dorn and Hanson, B032) ranks first on the common criteria. Identification credibility and attribution are strongest here. The local-labour-market import-exposure design is a joint product of the three credited names, and it has been re-examined for about a decade. As I recall, the qualitative finding of slow adjustment and concentrated, lasting local costs has survived that scrutiny. I have not verified this here. The citation should cover only the identified evidence on import competition, technology and local adjustment. It should not claim the task framework, which is shared with Levy, Murnane, Acemoglu, Restrepo and Katz, or any aggregate magnitude. The costs are the exclusion of Katz, the contested aggregate size and persistence of the effects, and some thematic proximity to recent labour and technology prizes. P002 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) is my strongest rival on breadth and maturity. Its unresolved choice between the theoretical originators and the estimation strand makes the credit more contestable. P004 follows because of its partly observational cross-country identification and its partial overlap with the 2024 prize. P001 is defensible on attribution, but the uncredited Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum lineage and the functional-form dependence of the welfare gains weigh against it. All four proposals are preferred to no award, because each rests on mature, consequential work.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile for P003: no documented co-authorship or institutional tie to Autor, Dorn, Hanson or Katz. Disclosures: my field (comparative democratisation, quality of government, V-Dem) is adjacent to P004, and I guarded against counting that familiarity as merit. I am a Stockholm University colleague, in a different department, of Hassler, Krusell and Boppart, who are relevant to P002 and P004. My 2024 presentation speech was delivered for the Academy and does not establish a personal prize preference. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
